title: Men of Soul: The 2000s
theme: The format's final commercial wave before solo artists and reality television fully took over — Jagged Edge and Ruff Endz carrying the genre's traditional sound into the new decade, B2K and Day26 representing two different routes into manufactured/televised groups, Pretty Ricky and the deep-cut acts Profyle and Prophet Jones rounding out the decade's quieter corners.
narrativePurpose: Close the Men of Soul series — and the combined ten-episode Ladies/Men of Soul arc — by tracing the 2000s male vocal group landscape through chart facts, label infrastructure, and the increasingly thin documentation of the format's final years.
toneProgression: The hits and chart records that defined the era → the labels, lineups, and reality-TV infrastructure behind the sound → the archival deep cuts and connective tissue closing out the series

vault.note: Digit 4 (index 3) is always visible. Vault code 2-0-0-0 — the year Jagged Edge's 'Let's Get Married' and Ruff Endz's 'No More' both broke through, opening the decade that would close out the format.

rounds.name: RADIO HITS
rounds.description: The hits and chart records that defined 2000s male vocal groups.

questions.question: Jagged Edge's April 2000 single, co-produced by Jermaine Dupri and Bryan-Michael Cox and written by the Casey brothers themselves, spent three weeks at #1 R&B and reached #11 Hot 100. What was it?

metadata.fact: 'Let's Get Married,' released April 11, 2000 on So So Def/Columbia, was co-produced by Jermaine Dupri and Bryan-Michael Cox and written by Brandon and Brian Casey — spending three weeks at #1 on the R&B/Hip-Hop chart and reaching #11 on the Hot 100.
metadata.storyHook: Three weeks at #1 R&B. Written by the group's own twins. 'Let's Get Married' opened the decade as Jagged Edge's signature statement.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Let's Get Married' (April 11, 2000, So So Def/Columbia), co-produced by Jermaine Dupri/Bryan-Michael Cox, written by Brandon/Brian Casey, 3 weeks #1 R&B, #11 Hot 100. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let%27s_Get_Married_(Jagged_Edge_song), Decked Out Magazine https://deckedoutmagazine.com/2026/05/15/jagged-edge-lets-get-married-history/

sources.title: Let's Get Married (Jagged Edge song) – Wikipedia
Jagged Edge: 'Let's Get Married' (2000) – Decked Out Magazine

questions.question: R&B duo Ruff Endz scored a 2000 hit, reaching #5 on the Hot 100, with which single?

metadata.fact: 'No More' (2000), from Ruff Endz's album Love Crimes, became the duo's signature hit — reaching #5 on the Hot 100 and the Top 20 on the R&B chart.
metadata.storyHook: #5 on the Hot 100. Ruff Endz's biggest crossover moment, right at the start of the decade.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'No More' (2000) from Love Crimes, #5 Hot 100, Top 20 R&B. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_More_(Ruff_Endz_song)

questions.question: B2K's 2002 single, featuring P. Diddy, reached #1 on the Hot 100. What was it?

metadata.fact: 'Bump, Bump, Bump' (2002), featuring P. Diddy, reached #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and was a major R&B chart hit — B2K's biggest commercial moment.
metadata.storyHook: #1 on the Hot 100. 'Bump, Bump, Bump' with P. Diddy was B2K's complete commercial breakthrough.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Bump, Bump, Bump' (2002) featuring P. Diddy, #1 Hot 100. Sources: German Wikipedia https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bump,_Bump,_Bump, Omarion Simple English Wikipedia https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omarion

questions.question: Jagged Edge's 2001 follow-up spent two weeks at #1 R&B and reached #9 on the Hot 100. What was it titled?

metadata.fact: 'Promise' (2001) spent two weeks at #1 on the R&B/Hip-Hop chart and peaked at #9 on the Hot 100 — confirming Jagged Edge as a sustained commercial presence rather than a one-hit act.
metadata.storyHook: Two weeks at #1 R&B. 'Promise' proved 'Let's Get Married' wasn't a fluke.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Promise' (2001), 2 weeks #1 R&B, #9 Hot 100. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promise_(Jagged_Edge_song)

questions.question: Miami group Pretty Ricky scored a 2005 breakthrough, reaching #7 on the Hot 100, with which single?

metadata.fact: 'Grind With Me' (2005) was Pretty Ricky's breakthrough hit, peaking at #7 on the Billboard Hot 100 and Top 10 on the R&B chart — establishing the Miami group within the decade's mid-period R&B landscape.
metadata.storyHook: #7 on the Hot 100. 'Grind With Me' put Pretty Ricky and Miami's R&B scene on the national map.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Grind With Me' (2005), #7 Hot 100, Top 10 R&B. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grind_With_Me

questions.question: Which B2K member served as the group's lead vocalist and frontman?

metadata.fact: Omarion served as B2K's lead vocalist and frontman, later launching a solo career after the group's run.
metadata.storyHook: Omarion was the voice out front on every B2K hit, before stepping into his own solo career.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Omarion was B2K's lead vocalist/frontman. Sources: Simple English Wikipedia https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omarion, Last.fm biography https://www.last.fm/music/Omarion/+wiki?ver=5

questions.question: Jagged Edge's lineup included a set of identical twins. What were their names?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 1 OF 3 — THE TWIN BROTHERS IN JAGGED EDGE

metadata.fact: Brandon Casey and Brian Casey, identical twins, were two of Jagged Edge's four members — alongside Richard Wingo and Kyle Norman, in a group formed in Atlanta in 1995.
metadata.storyHook: Identical twins, fronting an R&B quartet. Brandon and Brian Casey were the constant at the center of Jagged Edge.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Brandon and Brian Casey are identical twins and Jagged Edge members. Source: Genius artist bio https://genius.com/artists/Jagged-edge

reserve.question: Marques Houston, Jerome Jones, and Kelton Kessee rebranded their group from Immature to which name in 1999?

metadata.fact: Immature — Marques 'Batman' Houston, Jerome 'Romeo' Jones, and Kelton 'LDB' Kessee — rebranded as IMx in 1999 to reflect a more mature sound, releasing Introducing IMx (1999) and IMx (2001).
metadata.storyHook: 1999. The same three guys, but 'Immature' didn't fit anymore. IMx was the more grown-up name for a more grown-up sound.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Immature rebranded as IMx in 1999. Source: Facebook flashback post https://www.facebook.com/100086181999265/posts/formed-in-los-angeles-in-1991-and-managed-by-chris-stokes-the-american-rb-boy-ba

reserve.question: Ruff Endz, known for 'No More,' consisted of which two singers?
choices: David Davinch Chance and Dante Chi Jordan

metadata.fact: Ruff Endz consisted of David 'Davinch' Chance and Dante 'Chi' Jordan, an R&B duo who scored their biggest hit with 'No More' in 2000.
metadata.storyHook: Davinch and Chi. Two voices, one duo — Ruff Endz's entire identity.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Ruff Endz was David 'Davinch' Chance and Dante 'Chi' Jordan. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruff_Endz

reserve.question: Pretty Ricky, known for 'Grind With Me,' formed in which American city?

metadata.fact: Pretty Ricky formed in Miami, Florida — placing them within the city's broader 2000s R&B and hip-hop scene rather than the Atlanta-centered infrastructure that had dominated the prior decade.
metadata.storyHook: Miami, not Atlanta. Pretty Ricky's sound came out of a different city's scene entirely.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Pretty Ricky formed in Miami. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pretty_Ricky

reserve.question: Jagged Edge's biggest hits were produced by which Atlanta-based hitmaker, also responsible for launching Xscape a decade earlier?

metadata.fact: Jermaine Dupri produced Jagged Edge's biggest hits through his So So Def label — the same producer and label that had launched Xscape a decade earlier in the 1990s.
metadata.storyHook: Jermaine Dupri built two different eras of Atlanta R&B with his own hands — Xscape first, then Jagged Edge.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Jermaine Dupri produced both Xscape (1990s) and Jagged Edge (late 1990s/2000s) via So So Def. Sources: Wikipedia (Dupri production discography) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jermaine_Dupri_production_discography, Genius (Jagged Edge bio) https://genius.com/artists/Jagged-edge

rounds.name: DEEP CUTS
rounds.description: The labels, lineups, and reality-TV infrastructure behind the 2000s male vocal group sound.

questions.question: Day26 was formed in 2007 through which MTV reality competition series?

metadata.fact: Day26 was formed in 2007 by Sean Combs on the MTV reality show Making the Band 4 — the original lineup consisting of Robert Curry, Brian Angel, Willie Taylor, Qwanell 'Que' Mosley, and Michael McCluney.
metadata.storyHook: 2007. Five guys assembled on camera, on MTV, by Sean Combs — the same reality-TV formula that had created Danity Kane two years before.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Day26 formed 2007 by Sean Combs on Making the Band 4; lineup Robert Curry, Brian Angel, Willie Taylor, Qwanell Mosley, Michael McCluney. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Day26

questions.question: B2K recorded their catalog, including 'Bump, Bump, Bump,' for which label?

metadata.fact: B2K's releases were issued through Epic Records (via Sony) during their early-2000s run — the same label that also released Ruff Endz's catalog.
metadata.storyHook: Epic Records. Same label home for both B2K and Ruff Endz — two very different sounds, one shared roster.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: B2K recorded for Epic Records. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B2K

questions.question: How many members made up Jagged Edge's classic lineup?

metadata.fact: Jagged Edge's classic lineup consisted of four members — Richard Wingo, Kyle Norman, and identical twins Brian Casey and Brandon Casey — formed in Atlanta in 1995.
metadata.storyHook: Four voices. Two of them sharing the exact same face. Jagged Edge's lineup never needed a fifth.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Jagged Edge's classic lineup was Richard Wingo, Kyle Norman, Brian Casey, and Brandon Casey, formed in Atlanta in 1995. Sources: Genius bio https://genius.com/artists/Jagged-edge, YouTube documentary https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NtUVzbKZhFE

sources.title: Hollywood Insiders: The Unbreakable Legacy of Jagged Edge – YouTube

questions.question: Ruff Endz's 2000 hit 'No More' came from which album?

questions.question: Day26 was developed and produced by which entertainment mogul, who also created Danity Kane through the same reality TV format?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 2 OF 3 — THE PRODUCER BEHIND DAY26 AND DANITY KANE

metadata.fact: Sean Combs developed and produced Day26 through Making the Band 4 in 2007 — the same reality-TV format he had used to create Danity Kane two years earlier.
metadata.storyHook: Two groups, same formula, same producer. Sean Combs built Danity Kane and Day26 on the exact same reality-TV blueprint, just two years apart.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Sean Combs created Day26 via Making the Band 4, having previously created Danity Kane via Making the Band 3. Source: Wikipedia (Day26, creation by Sean Combs) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Day26
metadata.hostNote: Sean Combs has been subject to significant ongoing federal legal proceedings. The question addresses only his historical role producing Making the Band 4 and Day26 in 2007 — not any subsequent legal matters.

questions.question: Jagged Edge was discovered when a member of which 1990s female group slipped their demo to Jermaine Dupri — the same producer who had launched that group a decade earlier?

metadata.fact: Jagged Edge was discovered when Kandi Burruss of Xscape — the group Jermaine Dupri had launched with So So Def in the early 1990s — slipped their demo to Dupri, leading him to sign and produce them.
metadata.storyHook: Kandi Burruss handed Jermaine Dupri a demo tape. That tape was Jagged Edge — discovered by the same producer, through the same label, a decade after he'd built Xscape.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Jagged Edge discovered via Kandi Burruss slipping their demo to Jermaine Dupri, who had launched Xscape via So So Def. Sources: Wikipedia (Xscape) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xscape_(group), Wikipedia (Dupri production discography) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jermaine_Dupri_production_discography

questions.question: Prophet Jones member Jerome Goldee Lattisaw was the brother of which R&B singer?

metadata.storyHook: Prophet Jones barely made a dent commercially. But one member, Jerome 'Goldee' Lattisaw, had a sister who'd already made R&B history: Stacy Lattisaw.

questions.question: Prophet Jones, a male R&B/hip-hop vocal quartet active around 2000-2002, formed in which American city?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 3 OF 3 — PROPHET JONES'S HOME CITY

metadata.fact: Prophet Jones — Patrick 'P' Rowe, Kevin 'K.D.' Jackson, Tony 'Hollywood' Dumas, and Jerome 'Goldee' Lattisaw — formed in Washington, D.C., releasing their self-titled album in 2001 before disbanding shortly after.
metadata.storyHook: Washington, D.C. One self-titled album, in 2001. Prophet Jones came and went almost as quickly as they arrived.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified with caution — single niche-blog source: Prophet Jones formed in Washington, D.C. Source: Rare and Obscure Music blog https://rareandobscuremusic.wordpress.com/2017/01/14/prophet-jones/

reserve.question: Profyle, behind the 2000 hit 'Liar,' formed in which American city?

metadata.fact: Profyle, whose 2000 album Whispers in the Dark produced the hit 'Liar,' formed in San Francisco — a city outside the Atlanta-centered infrastructure that had defined so much of the prior decade's R&B vocal group scene. The group's momentum never carried into a follow-up hit.
metadata.storyHook: San Francisco, not Atlanta. Profyle's one hit, 'Liar,' came out of a city the era's R&B map usually skipped.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified with moderate confidence — origin city is less widely documented; San Francisco is repeated across niche R&B histories and matches prior EP017 sourcing, but isn't confirmed by a single authoritative primary source. Source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Profyle

reserve.question: Tony Hollywood Dumas and Jerome Goldee Lattisaw, both later in Prophet Jones, had previously been members of which 1990s R&B group together?

metadata.fact: Tony 'Hollywood' Dumas and Jerome 'Goldee' Lattisaw were both members of Me-2-U, a 1990s R&B group, before reuniting in Prophet Jones around 2000.
metadata.storyHook: Two members of Prophet Jones had already been in a group together once before — Me-2-U, a decade earlier.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified with caution — single niche-blog source: Dumas and Lattisaw were both Me-2-U members before Prophet Jones. Source: Rare and Obscure Music blog https://rareandobscuremusic.wordpress.com/2017/01/14/prophet-jones/
